lines.text: What happens if you pour straight diesel into a gas lawn mower?
It only runs while he sprays starting fluid and then it chokes on a cloud of white smoke.
Because a spark plug can't light diesel fast enough so the fuel just floods the cylinder unburned.
beats: ai:unburned liquid fuel pooling inside an engine cylinder around a spark plug macro

lines.text: Diesel engines skip the spark and squeeze the air so hard that it gets hot enough to ignite the fuel by itself.
beats: ai:a diesel engine piston compressing glowing hot air inside a cylinder cutaway
ai:fuel spray igniting by itself inside a red hot compressed cylinder

lines.text: But with half gas and half diesel the smoke clears and it mows the whole lawn.
And the compression even went up from 113 to 115 so the diesel didn't hurt anything.
Then he soaks cardboard in both fuels and lights them at the same time.
The gas bursts into flame and burns off fast while the diesel barely lights but then burns way longer.
That's why diesel trucks get better mileage because the fuel packs more energy and burns slow and steady.
beats: ai:a big diesel pickup truck driving down an open highway at sunset

lines.text: So would you ever try this in your mower?
